correctness.rationale: For n>=3, each matching rung is adjacent and dominates G_n, whereas each clique-internal edge omits a vertex of the opposite clique. A graph with at least six vertices, no universal vertex and total Roman weight four has an adjacent dominating pair: all feasible label multisets of weight <=4 are checked in RESULT.md. Edge deletion cannot create a new adjacent dominating pair. For k<n, minimum degree n prevents isolated vertices. Thus damaging deletions are precisely index-covering subsets. Untouched j-index sets permit (n-j)^2 edges, proving inclusion-exclusion exactly; equality and even/odd minimum multiplicities follow from the exhaustive classification of covers of n labels by rung singletons and two-index clique edges. Standalone checker exhaustively tested 459723 low-degree deletion sets for n=3,4,5,6, and directly optimized ternary labels on 743 deletions at n=3,4. Full proof, not finite verification, establishes all n and k in the stated ranges.

value.rationale: The total Roman domination edge-failure distribution is a graph reliability analogue quantifying, for every possible k-edge damage count below minimum degree, exactly how many failures force increased defense weight. For the unbounded two-clique prism family the complete coefficient profile has a compact inclusion-exclusion expression, and its minimum-deletion census separates odd path-plus-matching and rung-plus-matching types and supplies a parity-sensitive closed count. This is more informative than the mere bondage-number threshold, with exact conditional probabilities; the scope deliberately excludes isolation-capable k>=n.
